sections.Color & encoding: Panels a/b use discrete pale-to-navy blues with thresholds at 3/6/9/12% and an upper class >12%. Panel c uses red, blue and gray categories. Exact map colormap functions and hex colors are unverified.
sections.Design lessons: Use three maps with the same extent to compare two scenarios and their difference. Give continuous values and significance classes distinct legends. Label area percentages directly inside panel c.
sections.Statistics & symbols: Two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test, P < 0.05. Geographical-area-weighted shares: significantly positive 25.7%, significantly negative 11.3%, non-significant 63.0%.
sections.Verification & limitations: Reference-library reproduction, not a new analysis or causal validation. Read the source paper and complete Figure for context. Source version: Publisher Article in Press (licensed early version; not claimed to be final Version of Record).
sections.What the figure shows: Panels a/b map vegetation flash-drought sensitivity in early/late green-up years, as the median relative NDVI decline within 10×10-cell windows. Panel c classifies early-minus-late differences as significantly positive, significantly negative or not significant.

records.title: SHAP dependence, binned box plots and PDP insets
records.paper: Earlier green-up exacerbates northern vegetation sensitivity to flash drought
records.author: Wenrui Bai; Quansheng Ge; Constantin M. Zohner; Jun Wang; Shaozhi Lin; Yani Liang; Yongshuo H. Fu; Huanjiong Wang

sections.Color & encoding: The source notes cite the authors’ Figure3.R: vegetation #A7D398, climate #74A3D4, drought #DD847E, background #E9D389 and soil #969696. Bin colors interpolate from #B7D4EA to #084A91. Points are darkgrey with alpha = 0.3, PDP lines red and bands lightgrey. These are code-snapshot parameters, not screenshot estimates.
sections.Design lessons: Use translucent points to retain the event distribution and box summaries for grouped medians and spread. Link predictor families with categorical colors. A zero line helps interpret contribution signs. Panel a spans the first two rows of a three-column, four-row grid. Insets in b/c/h are near the upper left; others are mostly upper right, positioned to use available space.
sections.Statistics & symbols: n = 470,057 grid-cell–flash-drought events from cells where sensitivity in early-green-up years is significantly higher than in late-green-up years. Boxes span the 25th–75th percentiles with median lines; whiskers reach extremes within 1.5 IQR. The caption describes the PDP gray band as ±1 SD. The public code uses yhat ± sd(yhat), the SD across predictions along the entire PDP curve, not pointwise confidence intervals.
sections.Verification & limitations: Reference-library reproduction, not a new analysis or causal validation. Read the source paper and complete Figure for context. Source version: Publisher Article in Press (licensed early version; not claimed to be final Version of Record).
sections.What the figure shows: Panel a ranks 23 predictors by mean absolute SHAP value, colored by vegetation, climate, drought, background and soil families. Panels b–k show SHAP dependence for 10 predictors. Continuous predictors use 10 equal-width bins across the displayed x range; h uses seven biome categories. Main y-axes show SHAP values. Inset Sen (%) values, including the red bars in h, are partial-dependence predictions of vegetation sensitivity.

records.title: Risk-ratio maps with regional donut insets
records.paper: Anthropogenic aerosol reduction contributes to faster flash drought onset in a changing climate
records.author: Jia Wei; Shuo Wang; Weiguang Wang; Jason A. Otkin; Diego G. Miralles; Amir AghaKouchak

sections.Color & encoding: Panel a has a blue–white–red diverging appearance centered at RR = 1. Panel b combines pale-to-dark blue map fills, gray donut backgrounds and dark rose arcs. Visible ticks 0.90–1.10 are not exact endpoints because the colorbar extends beyond them.
sections.Design lessons: Use 1 as the neutral reference for risk ratios. Summarize Low 40.1% / High 59.9% globally before regional donuts. Map fills and donuts carry different information.
sections.Statistics & symbols: RR = P_AA/P_NAT. The main text interprets 59.9% as the share of global land with anthropogenic-aerosol-driven acceleration. Regional percentages are interpreted jointly from text and figure as regional acceleration-risk area shares, not contributions to acceleration magnitude. Exact regional aggregation awaits author-code confirmation.
sections.Verification & limitations: Reference-library reproduction, not a new analysis or causal validation. Read the source paper and complete Figure for context. Source version: Publisher Article in Press (licensed early version; not claimed to be final Version of Record).
sections.What the figure shows: Panel a shows 1990–2019 flash-drought onset-speed risk ratios from AA-only-forced CMIP6 simulations; RR > 1 indicates elevated acceleration risk. Panel b combines observation-derived regional aerosol-effect trends with donuts and percentages describing regional acceleration-risk patterns.
